page_title: An easy tutorial about Sentiment Analysis with Deep Learning and Keras

summary.title: An easy tutorial about Sentiment Analysis with Deep Learning and Keras
summary.one_liner: You learn how to clean text, turn it into word embeddings, and build and compare LSTM, Bidirectional LSTM, and Conv1D networks in Keras for sentiment classification.
keywords: how to classify product reviews positive negative neutral
takeaways: Text must be cleaned (URLs, punctuation, case, stop-words) and converted to numeric sequences before a neural network can use it.
Word embeddings are dense vectors learned from scratch via a Keras Embedding layer, and padded 2D arrays feed the model.
A single LSTM and a Bidirectional LSTM are built and compared; the Bidirectional version gave about 0.3% more validation accuracy in the author's run.
A Conv1D model trains fast but overfits quickly on small data; its best validation accuracy was around 82%.

The author's best model (Bidirectional RNN) reached about 81% on positive, 80% on negative and 91% on neutral ratings in the confusion matrix, which he calls a baseline rather than production quality.
summary.summary: The tutorial walks through a sentiment analysis pipeline for three-class text (positive, negative, neutral). It covers basic text cleaning in Python, the idea of word embeddings, padding sequences to a 2D array, and an Embedding layer feeding into models. It then builds an LSTM, a Bidirectional LSTM, and a Conv1D network in Keras, using dropout, checkpoints, softmax, and categorical crossentropy, and compares their validation results. The author notes that little hyperparameter tuning was done and that the code is in a linked repository.
